white-beans.name: White beans

sections.whatItOffers: White beans are creamy, mild beans that give potassium (about 19% of the adequate intake in half a cup), iron and magnesium, with 8.7 g of protein and 5.6 g of fibre.
sections.howToEatIt: Simmer into soups and stews, mash into dips, or toss with olive oil, lemon and herbs for a salad.
sections.cycleRelevance: Iron needs are higher for women aged 19 to 50 (18 mg a day, against 8 mg for men), partly because of menstrual blood loss (NIH ODS), and that need applies every day of the month. White beans add plant iron, which is absorbed less readily than iron from meat; vitamin C in the same meal helps. We found no reliable research linking white beans to a particular phase of the cycle.

wild-rice.name: Wild rice

sections.whatItOffers: Wild rice is the seed of an aquatic grass, nutty and chewy. Half a cup cooked gives zinc and magnesium for about 83 calories, with about 3.3 g of protein.
sections.howToEatIt: Simmer until the grains split, then use in pilafs, soups and salads, or mix with brown rice.
sections.cycleRelevance: it is a whole grain that adds zinc and magnesium to a meal. We found no reliable research linking wild rice to a particular phase of the cycle.

yellow-bell-pepper.name: Yellow bell pepper

sections.whatItOffers: A yellow bell pepper is sweet and crunchy and exceptionally rich in vitamin C: ten strips supply about 96 mg, more than the 75 mg daily reference.
sections.howToEatIt: Slice raw for snacking and salads, roast until soft and sweet, or grill. Add strips to a bean or lentil dish for extra vitamin C.
sections.cycleRelevance: Plant iron is absorbed better when vitamin C is in the same meal (NIH ODS); yellow pepper strips are an easy way to add it. We found no reliable research linking yellow bell pepper to a particular phase of the cycle.
